label: Depression as a health loss (shared conversion)

rows.label: Disability weight of a moderate episode of major depressive disorder (GBD 2019)

source.title: Global Burden of Disease Study 2019 (GBD 2019) Disability Weights, IHME

rows.explainer: How much of a year of healthy life a year of moderate major depression costs, by the Global Burden of Disease weights. One of the three points the shared depression conversion is fitted to.

rows.label: Disability weight of a severe episode of major depressive disorder (GBD 2019)

source.title: Global Burden of Disease Study 2019 (GBD 2019) Disability Weights, IHME
source.note: Major depressive disorder, severe episode: 0.658 (0.477–0.807); the same figure as GBD 2016's, which Founders Pledge used.

rows.explainer: How much of a year of healthy life a year of severe major depression costs, by the Global Burden of Disease weights. Founders Pledge's mental health analyses start from it.

rows.label: Healthy years lost per PHQ-9 point of depression for a year

source.title: GBD 2019 disability weights for major depression placed on the PHQ-9 severity bands (Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams 2001, J Gen Intern Med 16(9):606–613)
source.note: Slope of a least-squares line through each GBD weight at the middle of its PHQ-9 band: mild 0.145 at 7 (band 5–9), moderate 0.396 at 14.5 (bands 10–14 and 15–19: GBD has no moderately severe level), severe 0.658 at 23.5 (band 20–27): 0.031 per point. Range: Founders Pledge's StrongMinds spread of the severe weight over the whole scale (0.658 / 27 = 0.0244) to SoGive's 23 points for a full healthy year (1 / 23 = 0.0435).

rows.explainer:
The one way the site turns a fall in depression, measured on the PHQ-9 questionnaire (0–27), into years of healthy life: each point less for a year is 0.031 of a healthy year. It is the Global Burden of Disease weights for mild, moderate and severe depression placed on the PHQ-9's severity bands, so a fall from severe to mild counts what GBD counts for that change.

Evaluators each used their own: Founders Pledge 0.658 / 27 = 0.024 for StrongMinds and 0.658 / 23.25 = 0.028 for Action for Happiness, SoGive 1 / 23 = 0.043 (a full healthy year at the score where most people would rather feel nothing). Those set the range. A model measuring depression in standard deviations multiplies by the spread of PHQ-9 scores in its own sample.

rows.label: Spread (standard deviation) of PHQ-9 depression scores among people starting therapy

source.title: SoGive, StrongMinds cost-effectiveness analysis (March 2024), from the METAPSY database of psychotherapy trials
source.note: Standard deviation of PHQ-9 scores of trial participants before treatment. The range is ours: samples in psychotherapy trials in low- and middle-income countries typically show 3.5 to 5.5 points.

rows.explainer:
Turns an effect measured in standard deviations of a depression scale into PHQ-9 points: one standard deviation is about 4.2 points among people starting therapy. Psychotherapy effects are reported in these units, by SoGive (StrongMinds) and by the Happier Lives Institute, whose meta-analyses pool depression scales the same way.

With the shared 0.031 healthy years per point for a year, one standard deviation of depression for a year is 0.13 healthy years. That is the anchor the WELLBY exchange rate is calibrated on ("1 point more life satisfaction for a year vs doubled-income year"), so a fall in depression counts the same in HLI's analyses as in Founders Pledge's and SoGive's.
